announced.quote: Today at an international dark matter conference (IDM 2016) in Sheffield, UK

claim.quote: At a WIMP mass of 50 GeV/c^2, WIMP-nucleon spin-independent cross sections above 2.2e-46 cm^2 are excluded at the 90% confidence level. When combined with the previously reported LUX exposure, this exclusion strengthens to 1.1e-46 cm^2 at 50 GeV/c^2.

date.note: Announcement date: the SURF press release of 21 July 2016 says LUX scientists presented their results 'today' at the international dark matter conference IDM 2016 in Sheffield, UK. The arXiv v1 submission followed on 27 August 2016 and the paper was published as Phys. Rev. Lett. 118, 021303 (2017).

key_value_text.value: Spin-independent WIMP-nucleon cross sections above 1.1×10⁻⁴⁶ cm² excluded at 90% CL at 50 GeV/c² for the complete LUX exposure (above 2.2×10⁻⁴⁶ cm² for WS2014-16 alone)

name: Results from a search for dark matter in the complete LUX exposure
notes: significance is null: this is an exclusion limit.

summary.plain: Using all the data LUX took, the team again found no sign of dark matter. The paper reports roughly fourfold improvement in sensitivity for high WIMP masses relative to the collaboration's previous results.
summary.technical: WS2014-16 exposure of 3.35×10⁴ kg day (332.0 live days, 11 Sep 2014 - 2 May 2016) in a dual-phase xenon TPC with 250 kg of active mass, combined with the earlier WS2013 exposure. No evidence of WIMP nuclear recoils; spin-independent WIMP-nucleon cross sections above 2.2e-46 cm² at 50 GeV/c² are excluded at 90% CL, strengthening to 1.1e-46 cm² when combined with the previously reported LUX exposure.

title: Results from a search for dark matter in the complete LUX exposure
why_it_matters: The paper reports the complete LUX exposure: no evidence of WIMP nuclear recoils, with roughly fourfold improvement in sensitivity for high WIMP masses relative to the collaboration's previous results.
